Fruit Trees furnishing fabric

Alexander Girard turns trees into symmetrical black stems hung with flat orange, pink, and olive circles, ovals, and squares on white cotton.

Source
Art Institute of Chicago: Fruit Trees (Furnishing Fabric), 1988.76
Creator
Alexander Girard
Made
1960
Style
Mid-century modern (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Playful, warm, folk, optimistic
Evidence
Inspected, in the scratchpad only, the Art Institute of Chicago image of 1988.76 at 843 × 574 px (the largest size the museum serves for this in-copyright object). The image shows a detail with four vertical repeats. Not stored.
Reviewed
28 September 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

The Art Institute of Chicago dates the fabric 1960 and describes it as cotton, plain weave, screen printed; designed by Alexander Girard (1907–1993) and produced by Herman Miller, Inc., Zeeland, Michigan. The piece measures 104 × 132.5 cm with a repeat of 58.8 × 30.8 cm. Credit line: Gift of Mr. and Mrs. Alexander Girard; Alexander Demond Fund. AIC 1988.76.

The museum’s API marks the object as not public domain.

Observed

  • The ground is white. Black stems branch symmetrically from a central trunk in each repeat, with small curled tips.
  • Fruit shapes hang from the branches: orange and pink circles, pale pink ovals, orange and pink squares and trapezoids, and olive-green ovals on the trunk.
  • The shapes are flat color with no outlines; the black line is only the stems.
  • The trees stand in vertical columns side by side, with narrow white gaps between them.

Why it belongs

Girard mixes circles and squares freely on a folk-like tree form. The palette is warm and saturated, but softened by the pale pink and the white ground.

This is the “pattern as a band” idea at textile scale: small flat shapes repeated in columns.

Borrow

Build a symmetric plant from a thin black stem and flat, unoutlined circles, ovals, and squares.

Use orange, pale pink, and olive together on white for a warm but light repeat.
